baseline-first.note: Set B binds most values to specific named elevations and captures the artwork note ('SEE ARTWORK PKG FOR SIZE & MOUNT LOCATIONS') plus several correctly located components (TV in C3, MWD01/MWD02 and P2 in the bedroom elevations, 9'-10 1/4" and 3'-6" in North Bedroom). Set A is dominated by unbound or trivial claims — 'Wall section', 'interior elevation', 'identifier W2', 'panel reference P2', 'WB/TV/MWD01 location: interior elevation' — that add little, and it repeats the same dimensions several times. B does misfire more often: it repeatedly conflates A1 South Bedroom with A3 West Bedroom ('SOUTH BEDROOM ELEVATION A3 WEST'), assigns 4 1/2" and 9'-11 1/2" to A3 when they belong to C1/C5, puts 8'-8" in West Bedroom (it is in C5), calls MWD01 a window model, and invents 'center point X'. On balance B's correct, well-bound claims (about 11) far outnumber A's (about 5), while A's failures are mostly vagueness rather than hard misreads.

variant-first.note: Set A binds several dimensions and components to the correct named elevations (North Living width 9'-11 1/2", the artwork 'SEE ARTWORK PKG' note, TV and the 3'-9 11/16" segments in West Living, MWD02 in South Bedroom, 9'-10 1/4" and P2 in North Bedroom), whereas Set B leaves most claims attached to vague entities like 'interior elevation', 'Wall section' or 'room elevation' and repeats the same dimensions. Set A does make clear errors: it repeatedly conflates 'A3 WEST' with the South Bedroom elevation, assigns 9'-2" to West Bedroom and 3'-6" to North Bedroom when those values belong to other elevations, and invents properties/conditions such as 'top trim width', 'center point X', 'upper wall' and 'presence: installed'. Set B's few solid claims (MWL01 in West Living, the 1/2"=1'-0" scale, West Living segment dimensions) are outweighed by its vague, duplicated and misbound entries (e.g. 'W2 depth 4 1/2"', 'Interior Elevation E', 7'-6" tied to North Bedroom).

baseline-first.note: Set B binds the section properties correctly: B1 FLOOR BEAM NEAR GRID 5 is W10X15 and the ROOF BEAM @ GRID 2,3,4,5 (E6) carries the ø 3" opening, whereas Set A assigns W8X13 to B1 and W10X15 to E6, both misbound. Set A also invents/misplaces values: 10'-0" is not a 'near Grid 5' dimension (it belongs to the GRID 6 detail), 8" is not in detail E6, and 5'-0" is the GRID 3 (B4) dimension, not GRID 4. Set B's only clear errors are the 2'-6" dimension attributed to Detail C4 (it appears in the GRID 6 & NEAR GRID 5 detail) and the invented 'top flange width' reading of a 2" offset in B4; the rest of its claims keep the right detail, value and offset/spacing conditions.

Both sets capture the core facts (finished floor 2' - 9 1/2" above grade 0' - 0", room contents of the Centre Module and Living Room sections, 3/8" = 1'-0" scales), and both repeat the same unsupported value 2' - 3 1/2" for the Living Room finished floor, which the page never states. Set A adds several misbound or unsupported claims: CENTRE MODULE located at grid 'K', Mechanical Room located in 'Building Section A302' (A-302 is the sheet number, not a section), plus trivial duplicates such as 'WEST MODULE location West' and generic 'building section contains room' entries. Set B keeps conditions and bindings tighter (Mechanical Room within Centre Module, section scales tied to markers A1/C1) and its only clear error is the 2' - 3 1/2" value. Overall B is the more faithful and less padded set.

variant-first.note: Both sets share the same misread of the Living Room finished floor as 2' - 3 1/2" when the sheet reads 2' - 9 1/2". Set A otherwise binds values correctly (section scales for A1 and C1, room containment in each section, Mechanical Room within the Centre Module, West Module adjacent to Centre Module) with supporting quotes. Set B adds several vague or misbound claims — CENTRE MODULE 'location K' (a grid line), Mechanical Room 'location Building Section A302' (a sheet number, not a location), 'WEST MODULE location West' (tautological), and generic 'building section contains room' entries — plus more duplicate claims. Set A is therefore more faithful and less padded.

baseline-first.note: Set A binds nearly all values correctly to their tags and rows (e.g., F2 faucet model BSP-L-65014LF-PC, MWD02/MWD01/MWL01 millwork dimensions, CW and EX/RF locations), with only truncated values ("TIERRA S", "PORCELA") as blemishes. Set B covers a good range and gets many items right (TV size, P1/P2/P3 paint data, revision 4 date, cooktop model/manufacturer), but it misreads the F2 faucet model as "SP-L-65014LF-PC", binds the quartz thickness 1-3/16" to PT1 tile, invents a WB material of accent paint (wall base is MDF with finish as noted on elevations), and truncates the sink manufacturer to "FR". Those misbound and invented claims make B less faithful than A, whose errors are limited to clipped value strings.

variant-first.note: Set A contains several substantive errors: it binds the quartz thickness 1-3/16" to PT1 (a 4"x12" tile), invents a WB material of 'ACCENT PAINT PRATT & LAMBERT STEEL WOOL 33-14' when the wall base finish is 'AS NOTED ON ELEVATIONS', truncates the SK sink manufacturer to 'FR', and drops the leading 'B' from the bathroom-vanity faucet model. Set B is largely faithful across equipment, plumbing, furniture and millwork rows (e.g., BSP-L-65014LF-PC with tag F2, MWD02/MWD01/MWL01 dimensions, VANITY & SINK quantity 1), with only truncated manufacturer/description values ('TIERRA S', 'PORCELA') as defects. B therefore has fewer wrong claims and no misbound or invented facts, while still covering the key schedule data.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures the full revision table (marks 1–5 with dates and descriptions), the lot number, and the client/project block, all of which Set B omits entirely despite being prominent on the sheet. Set B's core elevation and scale claims are accurate but largely duplicate each other, and it introduces 'Detail A1' claims with a fabricated quote ('Detail A1: 3/8" = 1'-0"') and a wrong entity type (A1 is a section, not a detail). Set A's errors are the invented 'Bedroom 4' adjacency claims (the 4 is a grid line) and a garbled C1 scale value ('3/8" 3/8" = 1'-0"'), but its broader, correct coverage of revisions and title-block data outweighs Set B's omissions.

variant-first.note: Set A is clean and accurate on the section scales, A1 subject, and grade/finished-floor elevations, but it repeats several claims (bedroom adjacency, grade level) and omits the entire five-entry revision block with its dates and descriptions. Set B captures that revision history plus the lot number and both section scales, giving it substantially more correct content overall. B's faults are localized: it twice invents "Bedroom 4" (the sheet only labels BEDROOM), garbles the C1 scale value as "3/8" 3/8" = 1'-0"", mislabels the client block as the project name, and adds two vague room-layout claims. A's only real defect is a non-verbatim quote ("Detail A1: 3/8" = 1'-0"") for the A1 scale.

baseline-first.note: Set A covers substantially more distinct and important facts from the page — title-block data (lot number, team name/address, copyright), the BOREALIS project name, both detail scales, the white thinset adhesive and floor build-up layers — while Set B omits all of these and repeats itself heavily (gable/steel L-bracket twice, curb width twice, glass tile brick layout three times, 3/8" wall tile twice). Set B does bind the 3" dimension to the shower pan curb and the edge strip to the laundry millwork more correctly than A. However, A's errors are limited to a few items (backsplash 'material' = white thinset, an invented 'direction E' on the substrate slope, the 3" bound to shower pan width, and P3 folded into the bracket name), whereas B loses much more coverage and still misbinds the 3" as shower pan width once and PT1 to the bathroom floor finish.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the tile dimensions, substrate slope, gypsum and porcelain thicknesses, gable finish/attachment, and blocking correctly, with only a few redundant or loose claims. Set B misbinds P3 into the gable attachment using a merged, non-verbatim quote, calls white thinset mortar the backsplash material, and invents a 'direction E' condition drawn from the sheet grid border. Both sets misread the 3\" curb dimension as shower pan width, but B has more misbound and unsupported claims overall, while A also misses the adhesive and title-block/scale facts B captures.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures more of the sheet's substantive specifications correctly — the A36 threaded rod, (1) 2-1/4" heavy hex nut, keeper plate, pin connection plate, 11" dia x 1/2" plate, A325 bolt, W8X10 beam and neoprene pad — while Set B invents or misreads several values (PL3-1/2X3-1/2X1 given thickness 1/2" and separately "length 1 inch" when 1 is the thickness, and the 12" elevation-difference accommodation restated as rod "length capacity"). Set B also misbinds L3X3X1/4 to the diagonal brace and HSS4X4X1/4 to a "bracing member," and adds unverifiable orientation attributes (vertical/horizontal) to bare dimensions. Set A's weaknesses are duplicated claims and several unbound "component | dimension" entries (1/4", 4 3/4", 1'-5 1/4", 3 1/2"), plus a fabricated join making the column cap plate L3X3X1/4 and a misread of "3X 1/4" as quantity 3. Set B does add useful facts A misses (28" dia plate, C3X6, 12" elevation difference, 2 5/16" teflon hole), but its misread values are more damaging.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the threaded-rod system well (2-1/4" dia., A36, varying lengths to accommodate up to 12" elevation difference) and correctly pairs plate diameters with thicknesses (11" and 28" dia. x 1/2"), plus T.O. steel, neoprene pad and grade/first-floor elevations; Set B omits the rod diameter and the 12" accommodation entirely. Set B's clear defects are worse: it calls L3X3X1/4 the column cap plate specification (that is a separate angle) and reads "3X 1/4"" as a diagonal-brace plate of 1/4" thickness in quantity 3, and it pads the set with four unbound "component/detail typ" dimension claims. Set A's main errors are two claims on PL3-1/2X3-1/2X1 (thickness given as 1/2" and "length" given as 1", when 1 is the thickness), plus a couple of vague or duplicated claims. Overall A is more faithful and better bound, though both sets miss facts the other captures (B's keeper plate, pin connection plate, heavy hex nut, A325 bolt, W8X10).

Set A repeats the same facts several times (W8X10 three times, 11"X3/8" plates four times, GRADE LEVEL 0" twice) and adds unsupported conditions or misbindings: the 2'-9 1/16" dimension is given invented conditions ("inner dimension", "from grade level to lower plate"), 1/4" is called a gap/offset on the West Roof Cantilever and a slope on the Floor Overhang, and HSS4X4X1/4 is bound to the East Roof Cantilever although it is labeled in the C5/A4 details. Set B keeps the elevations (GRADE LEVEL 0", FIRST FLR 2'-4", T.O. STEEL 11'-4"), the plate/angle/HSS sections and the title-block and revision data correctly, with fewer invented conditions. Set B is not clean either: its two "slope 1/4"" claims misread a weld/plate symbol, the support-plate thickness of 1/4" rests on a stitched-together quote (the plate is 11"X3/8"), and two bare "thickness 1/4"" claims are unbound. On balance B carries more correct, well-bound facts and fewer misreadings than A.

baseline-first.note: Set A generally keeps values attached to the correct member types and section designations (C3X6 channel, W10X15/W10X12 beams, L4X4X5/16 and L3X3X1/4 angles, PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2, HSS 4X4X1/4 with its keynote), with quotes that match the text layer. Set B invents properties and conditions not on the sheet — 'framing spacing' of 11 1/2" and 6", duct-opening 'clearance' of 5/8" 'bottom' and 1 3/8" 'right side', and 10" called the depth of a C3X6 (a 3-inch channel) — plus several redundant C3X6 and 1/4" repeats. Set A's weaknesses are vaguer entities ('structural element', 'Duct Framing Detail') and two misbindings: PL5X3/8 attributed to 'component B' (a detail bubble) and L4X4X5/16 called a roof framing member when it appears in the duct/floor framing details. Overall A is the more faithful set.

variant-first.note: Set B captures the sheet's scale notation (1 1/2" = 1'-0") and the section/plate designations (L3X3X1/4, L4X4X5/16, PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2, HSS 4X4X1/4, W10X15) with values and quotes that match the text layer. Set A repeats the same C3X6/HSS/W10X15 claims many times and adds unsupported interpretations, e.g. binding 10" as the depth of a C3X6 member and calling 5/8", 1 3/8", 11 1/2" and 6" duct-opening clearances or framing spacing with no such labeling in the source. B is not clean either: its 'component B' plate claim misreads the detail bubble label B as a component, and its clearance/gap and width attributions (1", 1 13/16", 1'-4") are speculative. Overall B is more faithful and less padded, so it wins.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds dimensions to the correct views and components (e.g., 6'-7 1/2" and 3'-3 3/4" to the North Island elevation, 2'-5 1/16" to the Laundry Millwork section, 8'-4" to the East Island elevation) and keeps material/finish notes like 3/4" MDF GABLE FIN. W/ P3 and the 1" either-side minimum clearance intact. Set A invents or misbinds several items: SK read as "skirt," a 6" dining-table clearance, a 4'-0" width for the DIRTT Breathe wall, a 3'-0" width for DW, and MWK04 as QZ, plus a bogus "inches" unit on a finish material. Set B is weaker on redundancy (three near-duplicate 2"x6" framing claims) and two unsupported MWK04 conditions (offset from dining table, "excluding 6\" offset"), but its errors are fewer and less fundamental.

variant-first.note: Set B captures the title-block and revision-table facts (client, website, BOREALIS name, revision descriptions/dates) plus well-bound claims like DINING TABLE data & power and the 1" minimum clearance, all supported by the page. Set A repeats the same 2"x6" framing fact three times and misbinds several dimensions (2' - 2 3/16" to East Island although it belongs to the island/laundry sections, 3' - 3 3/4" to a 'DW section', SK as a MWK04 component), and its East Island total length states 8 ft while quoting 8' - 4". Set B's errors are fewer: SK expanded to 'skirt' is invented, MWK04 labeled as QZ is misbound, and a couple of dimension-to-attribute bindings (dining table height, countertop thickness) are shaky. Overall B is more accurate and better conditioned.

baseline-first.note: Set B captures key components that Set A omits entirely (4 X 3/8" CAP PLATE, 1" PL, PL5x4x3/8" TYP) and generally binds values to identifiable parts (cap plate, pipe, angle bolts, PV post base plate) with plausible detail locations. Set A contains many vague or misbound claims (e.g. 'component | width | 3"', 'Detail | dimension | 1/4"', 'crane attachment | dimension | 3/8"', 'CRANE ATTACHEMENT C3 | dimension | 2" TYP') and repeats the same plate/angle callouts several times. Set B is not flawless: its 1'-8" claim adds an invented condition ('from T.O. STEEL to top of cap plate'), the 'base plate width offset' and 'edge distance' bindings are uncertain, and one bolt quote appends 'TYP' not present in the source string. Overall B is more faithful and complete.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the drawing's labels to the correct components and details (cap plate 4 x 3/8, 3/4" hole in A3, 1 1/2" hole, 5x4x3/8 plate, 1/2" PL TYP, 1" PL, 3" STD pipe, 3x3x1/4 angle with (2) 3/4" bolts) and keeps typical/detail qualifiers. Set B invents several bindings: the 2" TYP and 3" TYP dimensions belong to the A1 PV post detail but are labeled as C3 crane-attachment, plate and component widths, and a bare 3/8" is called a fillet weld size with no supporting quote. Set B also uses vague entities ('Detail', 'component', 'crane attachment dimension') and a truncated quote, while omitting the cap plate and 5x4x3/8 plate facts that A captures. A's only real weaknesses are two speculative PV-post base-plate attribute bindings (width offset, edge distance).

Set A is clean but narrow, covering only the finished-floor and grade-level elevations with several near-duplicate claims and omitting the drawing scale, revision history, and lot number. Set B captures those additional supported facts (both section scales, all five revision dates/descriptions, lot number 116) while keeping the same elevation claims correctly bound to the C1/A1 sections. Set B's only real defect is binding 'U.S. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY SOLAR DECATHLON 2013' to Project name when the title block lists it under CLIENT. Overall B is more complete and equally faithful.

baseline-first.note: Set A covers the revision history, section scales, project/client block, lot number, and the grade/finished-floor datums with quotes that match the page, whereas Set B only repeats the Grade Level and Finished Floor elevations seven times and omits all revisions, scales, and title-block facts. Set B's claims are accurate but near-duplicates, so its coverage misses most of the page's engineering content. Set A's only questionable item is labeling the client block 'Project | name'; otherwise its claims are supported and correctly bound.

Set A captures more genuinely supported facts — plate hole diameter and spacing, wood lag screw with washer, continuous sealant, grade-level elevation, and the 3/8" x 4" hex through bolt — with verbatim quotes. Set B duplicates the same frame/joist/bolt items repeatedly while omitting those facts, and it misbinds the 8'-0" and 1'-4" module dimensions to the A3 deck-module connection and fabricates quote text ("Detail A3: 3/4\" = 1'-0\" DECK MODULE TO CONNECTION", "3/4\" = 1'-0\" TYP.", "8 8D...", "OUGH BOLT"). Set A's main faults are misattributing the 1'-4 3/4"/1'-4"/1'-3 1/4" module segments to RAILING ATTACHMENT, calling 8'-0" a connection spacing, and an invented scaffold-footing-to-frame connection. On balance A is the more faithful and better-covered set.

variant-first.note: Set B preserves the specification conditions more faithfully (8D ring-shank nail @ 6" O.C. each side, lag screw with washer, plate holes typical, sealant each side as recommended by manufacturer) and adds real facts A misses (lag screw, sealant, 7/16" plate holes, grade level 0"), with verbatim quotes. Set A duplicates the frame/joist/hex-bolt claims three times each, misreads the callout number as "8 8D", and fabricates or truncates quotes ("3/4" = 1'-0" TYP.", "OUGH BOLT", "Detail A3: 3/4" = 1'-0" DECK MODULE TO CONNECTION"), while misbinding 8'-0" and 1'-4" to the A3 connection. B's main errors are misbinding the 1'-4 3/4" / 1'-4" / 1'-3 1/4" segment dimensions (A1 typ. deck module) to RAILING ATTACHMENT, calling 8'-0" a "deck connection spacing", and an unsupported scaffold-footing-to-frame connection plus two trivial tautological claims. B also omits the joist, steel decking and waterproofing membrane, but on balance its correct claims are more numerous and better bound.

baseline-first.note: Set A binds the level markers correctly as elevations (solar envelope 18'-0", finished floor 2'-9 1/2", grade 0'-0") and captures facts B omits, notably the 40-tube count from "2 X APSE-20 (40 TUBES)" and both General Sheet Note 3 items on door swing/tilt-and-turn operation. Set B adds the PV solar array and cable-railing material, but it re-labels the solar-envelope datum as a "height," invents a roof/upper-structure binding for the PV array, and asserts P1 is cement fibre board siding with a quote ("P1 CEMENT FIBRE BOARD SIDING") that does not appear in the source. Both sets are padded with near-duplicate handrail, cladding and finished-floor entries, so A's advantage rests on accuracy rather than coverage. A's only soft spot is the added condition "relative to Grade Level" on the finished-floor elevation, which is inferable from the drawing but not stated in its quote.

variant-first.note: Set A covers PV solar arrays and cable-railing material that Set B omits, but it introduces an unsupported P1 material claim with a fabricated quote and mislabels the South Elevation view as "Detail C1" for the W5/W6 location claims, while also repeating the solar-envelope, finished-floor, handrail and railing-post facts many times. Set B is cleaner and adds facts A misses (40-tube quantity, 2 x APSE-20 configuration, door swing/tilt-and-turn notes, grade level, window/door tag identifiers), with only a minor attribute mislabel of the 18'-0" solar envelope as an "elevation". B's main gap is the absent PV solar array, but overall it has fewer wrong and redundant claims while capturing slightly more of the sheet's key information.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures several specific, verifiable facts that B misses or mangles: the L3X3X1/4 support angle specification, the 3/8" through-bolt diameter, and the 1 1/2" = 1'-0" drawing scale, and it binds segment lengths (3'-8 3/8", 2'-11 7/8", 2'-3 7/8") to the correct module details. Set B invents property labels that the drawing does not support (web thickness and flange thickness for the 1 1/2" and 5/8" values, thickness 5/8" for Module A) and repeats the same 6", 2", and 4 3/4" values under several vague or duplicate labels. Both sets contain vague entities and duplicated claims, and A also has a misbinding (2'-3 7/8" attributed to MODULE B when it appears in the Module A detail), but B's invented thickness/offset properties and blanket 'Detail A1' conditions on values from the Module B detail are more damaging.

variant-first.note: Both sets contain vague or invented entities ("base block", "base component", bare "dimension" claims), but Set A repeats more of these and misbinds thickness-type attributes (e.g. "web thickness 1 1/2"", "flange thickness 5/8"", "thickness 5/8"") that the drawing does not support. Set B captures two important facts Set A omits entirely — the L3X3X1/4 support angle designation and the 1 1/2" = 1'-0" drawing scale — plus the 3/8" through-bolt diameter and correctly scoped segment lengths (3'-8 3/8", 2'-11 7/8"). Set B's main errors are the misbound 2'-3 7/8" attributed to Module B (it belongs to Module A) and the 5/8" "base offset" on the C1/S-301 reference, along with several invented base-block claims. Overall Set B has fewer unsupported bindings and more faithful, correctly scoped claims.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds its member sections to specific elevations/details (HSS4X4X1/4 in C3, HSS4X6X1/4 and L4X4X5/16 in C1, W8X10 in the North/Bedroom elevation) and correctly captures the bay 10'-0" (grid C-D), 7'-6" (grids 4-5), 32'-0", 27'-8", Solar Envelope 18'-0" and T.O. Steel 11'-4". Set A gets the datum elevations right (FIRST FLR 2'-4", T.O. STEEL 11'-4" above grade, SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0") and adds the 3'-1" B-C bay, but it also misbinds dimensions: it calls 9'-0" the grade-to-T.O.-steel height (contradicting the 11'-4" datum), restates 27'-8" as "27 ft" from grid 8 to 4, and labels 3" and 8'-8 5/8" as structural-member heights. Set B's weaknesses are two confused conditions (grid spacing "between C4 and Grid 6", span "between grid D and C1"), one vague 2'-0" height-segment claim, and three duplicated claims (12'-0", 18'-0", 27'-8"), but it has fewer outright misreadings than A.

variant-first.note: Set A binds section designations to the correct elevations/details more consistently (HSS4X4X1/4 in C3, HSS4X6X1/4 and L3x3x1/4" in C1, W8X10 in the North/Bedroom elevation, W10X12 in A1) and keeps the key datums (SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0", T.O. STEEL 11'-4", 32'-0", 27'-8", 7'-6", 12'-0", 10'-0") with supporting quotes. Set B adds the useful FIRST FLR 2'-4" datum but introduces clear errors: C4 is a detail/section callout not a column identifier, the 27'-8" dimension is restated as "27 ft", and 9'-0" is misbound as grade-to-T.O.-steel (that span is 11'-4"; 9'-0" is first floor to T.O. steel), plus several vague "Structural Member" claims. Set A's weaknesses are invented qualifiers ("right side upper", "rightmost", "Bracing member", "Lower beam", "between C4 and Grid 6", "between grid D and C1") and three duplicated claims, but its value-to-component binding is still more faithful overall.

Set B binds values to the correct sections and grids more consistently and preserves meaningful conditions (e.g., 2'-4" between GRADE LEVEL and FIRST FLR, 9'-0" from First Floor to T.O. Steel, 1'-3" and 8'-8 5/8" in Structural Section 2). Set A repeatedly attaches Section 4 dimensions (1'-8 7/16", 1'-8", 8", 10", W10X15) to "Detail A1", puts the 37'-6" overall span in Section 3 when it is in Section 1, and refers to grid "A4" (a section callout), plus duplicates and vague no-condition claims. Set B's errors are mainly the misread grid label "C1 to B", a 6" offset wrongly placed in Section 1, and the vague "Column A1 … to specific datum".

Set B captures more distinct, correctly bound facts from the sheet — 4x4 post "TO BE CUT AS NEEDED", the 3/4" x 5 1/2" reclaimed wood surface, bolt diameter/length/head type, and the 7 1/2" dimension bound to the joist — while Set A leaves those out and instead offers vague "upper component" claims and three near-duplicate 3 1/2" claims whose binding to "decking footing width" is unsupported. Both sets misattribute the 8'-0" dimension (it is the post height in detail A6, not C3 or C1), but Set A does so twice and also repeats FIRST FLR, 2" x 8" frame and the 18" title text several times. Set B's remaining faults (invented "span 5-6", "deck module section" for an A6 dimension, merged "nut sleeve", and the vague "threaded rod | connection | sleve") are fewer than Set A's misreadings and trivial title-derived claims.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds dimensions to the correct details more consistently: the 3/4" threaded rod, 2" x 8" joist, 3 1/2" footing plan dims and the 8'-0" span in the C3 footing elevation are all placed plausibly, and the 3/4" plywood thickness is read correctly. Set A invents an entity ('span 5-6'), misassigns 8'-0" to the C1 decking footing plan, merges '1" NUT' and 'SLEVE' into a nonexistent 'nut sleeve', and twice binds 3 3/4" (an A6 landscape-footing dimension) to the deck footing and the B4 deck module section. B's weaknesses are one misread (calling the 8'-0" span a height of 8 ft) and two vague 'upper component' claims, while A also carries more duplicate/trivial repeats. Both omit or blur some facts (A never states the 3/4" threaded rod; B never states the 4x4 post or 5 1/2" reclaimed surface), but B is the more faithful set overall.

variant-first.note: Set B captures several page facts A misses entirely — HSS4X4X1/4, the 3" DIAM STD. PIPE, the 14 GAUGE PLATE deck opening, and the '6" MIN EACH SIDE' reinforcement note — while A repeats the same W6X20, 1'-0" and 1/4" claims multiple times. A also invents two fitted-stiffener dimensions (3" 'total horizontal width' and 2" 'horizontal offset') that are actually foundation-detail dimensions, plus unsupported 'side/top fillet weld' and 'opening height' conditions. B's main faults are a misbound hole diameter (the (4) 3/4" holes belong to the wide-flange/base plate, not the fitted stiffener), W6X20 attributed to the PV attachment rather than the foundation detail, and an invented 'right' overlap condition. Both sets contain duplicates and vague 3/8" claims, but B's coverage of distinct correct facts outweighs its misbindings.

baseline-first.note: Set A makes several cross-elevation misbindings: 17'-3 1/8" (a kitchen width in A1/A4) is assigned to both the North Kitchen and North Bathroom elevations, 5'-8" and 8'-6 13/16" (A6 West Bathroom values) are bound to the North Kitchen and to "P3", 8'-6 1/2" is paired with the D1 "U/S OF FIN. CEILING" note although D1's height is 8'-1 7/8", and it invents an "Interior Elevation B" plus an unsupported "MWB03 above MWB02" location. Set B binds values to the correct elevations more often (South Bathroom overall width 10'-3 15/16", Base fin. W/ P3, DIRTT living wall 5'-6", MWB01 2'-6", mirror 2'-4", correct scales), though it also errs by tagging South Bathroom dims as "D5", putting 2'-6 3/8" (North Kitchen) on the West Bathroom, locating MWK01 in the West Bathroom, inventing an artwork "bottom to floor" condition, and giving "H1" as the robe hook height. B's remaining claims are largely redundant or trivial but fewer are flatly wrong or invented, and it recovers the South Bathroom width and base finish that A misses.
